description: REGRESSION WALL for saga #811, flipped by issue #815 from the characterization issue #816 built against the broken build. It asserts the CORRECT behaviour now: the check before execution runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 over the whole program and, on an `error`-severity finding, **Phase 2 never begins** — "no instruction executes, no trace event is emitted" (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`). So the `events` array is EMPTY, and that emptiness is the assertion: before the fix this program ran, produced events, and reported nothing, which is the silent wrong answer the saga is named for. Reverting the gate turns this red. Fault shape A — an UNRESOLVABLE NAME in argument position. `check()` always computed the right answer (`ol-unknown-command`, whose usual stage is `semantic` per spec/error-model.md:97); what #815 changed is that `execute()` now consults it, so the fault reaches the learner instead of the statement being discarded whole. The end-to-end shape of saga #811's headline evidence, measured on a program that is actually in this repository (see the `-check` sibling on why the maintainer's `PLANT` fractal is not). `tree` recurses through an argument holding an unresolvable name. Before the fix the drawing collapsed to its first level — ONE `procedure-enter` and TWO `draw-segment` events, against the FOUR and SIX its `recursion-baseline-unaffected` twin produces from the identical program with `(:n - 1)` in place of `(wibble :n)` — with zero diagnostics on both sides: a learner saw a stub drawing and was told nothing. Now it draws NOTHING and says why, while the baseline twin stays byte-for-byte unchanged. That pair is the fix stated as a diff: one column moves, the other must not.
